 ===== grok worker controller --help =====
 Claim pending Cloud Agent requests for team pools and run a spawn hook for each.
 
-Watches the pending-request stream of each `--pool` (or the whole team with `--all-pools`), claims each new request for a fresh worker id, and runs `--spawn` once per claim. The hook gets `CURSOR_AGENT_WORKER_ID`, `CURSOR_POOL`, `CURSOR_API_KEY` (or `CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN` with `--session-token`) and the request's fields, and should start `grok worker --pool "$CURSOR_POOL" start` somewhere. A sleeping machine in a pool with a wake window runs the hook again with `CURSOR_WAKE=1`, `CURSOR_WAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` and its own worker id, without a claim. Logs go to stderr at info level; `RUST_LOG` overrides that. Authenticates with a team service account key (`--api-key` or `CURSOR_API_KEY`).
+Watches the pending-request stream of each `--pool` (or the whole team with `--all-pools`), claims each new request for a fresh worker id, and runs `--spawn` once per claim. The hook gets `CURSOR_AGENT_WORKER_ID`, `CURSOR_POOL`, `CURSOR_API_KEY` (or `CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN` with `--session-token`) and the request's fields, and should start `grok worker --pool "$CURSOR_POOL" start` somewhere. That worker needs Grok Build unified: start it with `GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1` unless the build embeds the agent-host daemon. A sleeping machine in a pool with a wake window runs the hook again with `CURSOR_WAKE=1`, `CURSOR_WAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` and its own worker id, without a claim. With `--warm-idle` the controller never claims: it keeps idle workers connected in each `--pool`, and the server assigns queued requests to them. Logs go to stderr at info level; `RUST_LOG` overrides that. Authenticates with a team service account key (`--api-key` or `CURSOR_API_KEY`).
 
 Usage: grok worker controller [OPTIONS] --spawn <PATH>

@@ -274,6 +307,16 @@
           
           `CURSOR_WORKER_POOL_NAME` names the pool of a bare `--pool` or `--single-use` and is ignored otherwise.
 
+      --mint-github-token
+          Let Cursor send the pool worker short-lived GitHub tokens during a claimed run.
+          
+          Needs `--pool`. A team admin must turn on GitHub token minting for pool workers. Without this flag, the worker refuses the tokens. The worker redacts the token from what the agent sees, best effort.
+
+      --warm-idle <COUNT>
+          Keep this many idle workers connected in each `--pool`, without claiming.
+          
+          Runs `--spawn` once per missing worker, with a fresh `CURSOR_AGENT_WORKER_ID`, the pool, the API key and the `--repository` if one is given, and no request; the server assigns queued requests to the idle workers. Idle counts come from the team's pool stats, read every minute and after stream events. At most 100. Needs `--pool`; cannot be combined with `--all-pools`, `--session-token` or `--identity-audience`. Run one warm controller per pool: without claims, two can spawn more workers than needed.
+

           Cursor public API base for the claim calls and the hook's `CURSOR_API_URL`.

@@ -336,6 +374,16 @@
           
           ADDRESS is `:8080` (every IPv4 address) or `host:8080`. `GET /healthz` answers 200 while the worker runs, and 503 once it has stopped for good (a rejected credential). `GET /readyz` answers 200 when the worker is connected to Cursor, holds no claim and is not shutting down, and 503 otherwise; its JSON body reports each of those. The worker fails to start when it cannot bind ADDRESS. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`).
 
+      --run-mcp-servers
+          Run each Cloud Agent's stdio MCP servers on this pool worker.
+          
+          A personal worker always runs them, as the Cursor CLI's does. A pool worker runs them only with this flag, because they are commands from any member of the team. They start in the claim's worktree with its environment, without the worker's Cursor credentials. A worker that runs them also offers every claim the stdio servers in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, as the Cursor CLI's does. Needs `--pool` or `--single-use`.
+
+      --mcp-tool-timeout <SERVER[/TOOL]=SECONDS>
+          How long a tool call to a stdio MCP server this worker runs may take. Repeatable.
+          
+          `SERVER=SECONDS` covers every tool of that server; `SERVER/TOOL=SECONDS` covers one tool and wins over the server's value. A later value for the same server or tool replaces an earlier one, and `0` fails each call without waiting. SERVER is the name in the claim's MCP config, which the worker logs when it starts the server. Without it a call fails after the MCP SDK's 60 seconds; Cursor itself stops waiting after about 14 minutes. A `--pool` worker also needs `--run-mcp-servers`. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`).
+
       --idle-release-timeout <SECONDS>
           Seconds a claim may sit idle before Cursor releases it. 0 turns this off.
           
@@ -343,6 +391,16 @@
           
           [env: CURSOR_WORKER_IDLE_RELEASE_TIMEOUT=]
 
+      --data-dir <DIR>
+          Directory for this worker's state, served by its own leader.
+          
+          Holds the worker ids, Cursor session, claim worktrees and clones that otherwise live in the Grok home, so it must be another directory. The leader listens at `DIR/leader.sock`, so each data directory runs one worker, as in the Cursor CLI; `--leader-socket` cannot name another socket. `grok worker status` and `stop` with the same directory reach that leader. Unlike the Cursor CLI, `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` is not read. Needs the agent-host backend (`GROK_AGENT_HOST_BACKEND=1`), as does `--wait`.
+
+      --wait [<SECONDS>]
+          Wait for the leader already running on the worker's socket to stop, then start.
+          
+          The socket is `--data-dir`'s, else `--leader-socket`, else the default one that every `grok --leader` shares, whose leader stays up while any of them is connected. Without SECONDS, waits as long as it takes; with SECONDS, fails once they pass. Without `--wait`, `start` leaves a running leader alone.
+

           Enable debug logging
